entities.summary:
Jacob Senleches was a Franco-Flemish composer and harpist of the late Middle Ages, known for his contributions to the ars subtilior style. Born in the 14th century, Senleches' music has been preserved through various manuscripts and performances by later musicians.

He was a prominent figure in the Franco-Flemish court music tradition, collaborating with other notable composers such as Guillaume Dufay and Johannes Ockeghem. Senleches' compositions were characterized by their intricate harmonies and complex rhythms, which influenced the development of polyphonic music in Europe.

Despite his significant contributions to the musical landscape of the late Middle Ages, Senleches' life and work are not well-documented in modern historiography. However, his music continues to be performed and studied by scholars and enthusiasts alike, providing a fascinating glimpse into the cultural and artistic achievements of this pivotal era.

The ars subtilior style, which Senleches helped to popularize, had a lasting impact on the evolution of Western classical music. Its influence can be seen in the works of later composers, such as Josquin des Prez and Palestrina, and continues to inspire musicians and musicologists today.
